question: Will the price of regular unleaded gas in the U.S. reach $5 a gallon before election day 2026, according to AAA?

calls.reasoning: AAA national average was $4.33 on 2026-10-14, down from $4.37 a week earlier, with crude above $106 because of the Iran war and Hormuz disruptions. Reaching $5.00 needs +15.5% (+$0.67) by Nov 2, at most 16 days. The 2022 analog: a ~$0.72 jump in about 10 days happened only on a fresh supply shock (Ukraine invasion), and the $5.01 record peak came months later. The status quo is flat-to-falling prices. A Manifold market on the AAA average hitting just $4.50 before Nov 3 is at 11% (small volume), so $5 sits much further in the tail. The residual comes from a sudden Hormuz escalation. Live web tools failed this run, so evidence is thin and limited to the prompt's material.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs used the same evidence (AAA $4.33 on Oct 14, $4.37 a week before, crude >$106, record $5.016 in June 2022) and each issued 0.02. The only factual differences are the quoted starting level for the March 2022 surge ($3.53/$3.54/$3.61); every version is about +20-23% in two weeks after a fresh shock, so the conclusion doesn't change. No run retrieved Oct 15-16 AAA readings or post-Oct-14 news, and I couldn't either (no web access); that is unresolved uncertainty, kept as tail mass. The remaining dispute is judgment, about how much the active war fattens the tail. Estimate: P(major escalation within ~2 weeks) ~5-8%, times P(reaching $5 by Nov 2 | escalation) ~30%, gives ~2%. The Manifold $4.50 contract (0.11, same source and deadline, lower threshold) is consistent with this.
